name: Hymenaeus, Alexander, and Philetus
charge: Making shipwreck of the faith; blasphemy; teaching that the resurrection is past already
summary: Paul charged Timothy to hold faith and a good conscience, which some had put away and so made shipwreck concerning the faith, naming Hymenaeus and Alexander, whom he delivered to Satan that they might learn not to blaspheme (1 Timothy 1:19-20). The error is named in the second letter: the word of Hymenaeus and Philetus ate as a canker, and they erred concerning the truth, saying that the resurrection was past already, and overthrew the faith of some (2 Timothy 2:16-18).
offenseFull: Paul set two words beside each other on purpose. Some had swerved and turned aside to vain jangling (1 Timothy 1:6), and some had put away faith and a good conscience and made shipwreck (1 Timothy 1:19). Swerving and putting away are the same motion: men walking away from a truth they once had. The charge does not come from a man who had never been wrong. Paul had just finished telling Timothy that he was before a blasphemer, a persecutor, and injurious, who shut up the saints in prison, gave his voice against them when they were put to death, punished them often in every synagogue and compelled them to blaspheme, and obtained mercy because he did it ignorantly in unbelief (1 Timothy 1:13; Acts 26:10-11).

The doctrine itself is identified: their word would eat as a canker, and Hymenaeus and Philetus, concerning the truth, had erred, saying that the resurrection was past already, and overthrew the faith of some (2 Timothy 2:17-18). These men had rolled with Paul. The obvious question is how a man goes from strong in the gospel to speaking heresy, and the answer is that somebody got into his ears. Paul never taught it, and he had to spend a whole chapter with the Corinthians proving from what he himself had received and delivered that Christ died, was buried, rose the third day, and was seen of Cephas, then of the twelve, then of above five hundred brethren at once (1 Corinthians 15:3-8,12). That is why Timothy is told to shun profane and vain babblings, which increase to more ungodliness, and to charge men not to strive about words to no profit, because such talk subverts the hearers (2 Timothy 2:14-16). Shut it down immediately and give it no place, not for an hour, which is exactly what Paul did with the false brethren brought in privily at Jerusalem (Galatians 2:4-5).
judgmentFull: Paul delivered Hymenaeus and Alexander to Satan, that they might learn not to blaspheme (1 Timothy 1:20). It is the same sentence passed on the man at Corinth and it means the same thing: put out of the assembly (1 Corinthians 5:5). A man who will not be corrected is cut off so that what he carries stops spreading, and a man that is a heretick, after a first and second admonition, is to be rejected, being subverted and condemned of himself (Titus 3:10-11). Mark them which cause divisions and offences contrary to the doctrine, and avoid them (Romans 16:17).

The remedy Paul gives the rest of the congregation is a house with vessels in it. In a great house there are not only vessels of gold and silver but also of wood and of earth, some to honour and some to dishonour, and the man who purges himself from these is a vessel to honour, sanctified and fit for the master’s use and prepared to every good work (2 Timothy 2:20-21). Hymenaeus and Philetus are the examples of what to purge yourself from, because God cannot use a man tangled up with them. What Timothy heard was to be committed to faithful men, which is to say loyal ones (2 Timothy 2:2). And the foundation of God stands sure with its seal, that the Lord knows them that are his, and that every one that names the name of Christ is to depart from iniquity (2 Timothy 2:19). Alexander does not disappear from the record here; Paul warns of him again in the last chapter he ever wrote (2 Timothy 4:14-15).

taught.title: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

lawsResolved.text: We should give no occasion for blasphemy to occur.
Beware lest any deceive you through philosophy, according to the traditions of men, and not according to Christ.
Let no one deceive you by any means that would cause you to depart from the faith.
Reject a heretick and factious man after the first and second admonition, knowing that such a man is perverted and lost in sin, being self-condemned.

text.text: From which some having swerved have turned aside unto vain jangling;
Holding faith, and a good conscience; which some having put away concerning faith have made shipwreck:
Of whom is Hymeneus and Alexander; whom I have delivered unto Satan, that they may learn not to blaspheme.
Who was before a blasphemer, and a persecutor, and injurious: but I obtained mercy, because I did it ignorantly in unbelief.
Which thing I also did in Jerusalem: and many of the saints did I shut up in prison, having received authority from the chief priests; and when they were put to death, I gave my voice against them.
And I punished them oft in every synagogue, and compelled them to blaspheme; and being exceedingly mad against them, I persecuted them even unto strange cities.
And their word will eat as doth a canker: of whom is Hymeneus and Philetus;
Who concerning the truth have erred, saying that the resurrection is past already; and overthrow the faith of some.
For I delivered unto you first of all that which I also received, how that Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures;
And that he was buried, and that he rose again the third day according to the scriptures:
And that he was seen of Cephas, then of the twelve:
After that, he was seen of above five hundred brethren at once; of whom the greater part remain unto this present, but some are fallen asleep.
After that, he was seen of James; then of all the apostles.
And last of all he was seen of me also, as of one born out of due time.
Now if Christ be preached that he rose from the dead, how say some among you that there is no resurrection of the dead?
Of these things put them in remembrance, charging them before the Lord that they strive not about words to no profit, but to the subverting of the hearers.
Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth.
But shun profane and vain babblings: for they will increase unto more ungodliness.
And that because of false brethren unawares brought in, who came in privily to spy out our liberty which we have in Christ Jesus, that they might bring us into bondage:
To whom we gave place by subjection, no, not for an hour; that the truth of the gospel might continue with you.
To deliver such an one unto Satan for the destruction of the flesh, that the spirit may be saved in the day of the Lord Jesus.
A man that is an heretick after the first and second admonition reject;
Knowing that he that is such is subverted, and sinneth, being condemned of himself.
Now I beseech you, brethren, mark them which cause divisions and offences contrary to the doctrine which ye have learned; and avoid them.
But in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and of silver, but also of wood and of earth; and some to honour, and some to dishonour.
If a man therefore purge himself from these, he shall be a vessel unto honour, sanctified, and meet for the master’s use, and prepared unto every good work.
And the things that thou hast heard of me among many witnesses, the same commit thou to faithful men, who shall be able to teach others also.
Nevertheless the foundation of God standeth sure, having this seal, The Lord knoweth them that are his. And, Let every one that nameth the name of Christ depart from iniquity.
Alexander the coppersmith did me much evil: the Lord reward him according to his works:
Of whom be thou ware also; for he hath greatly withstood our words.
